mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in a month indicates a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of falling unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong GDP growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which increases input costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of decreasing industrial production compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% in a month signals a strengthening housing market, which boosts related industries and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increasing housing starts compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong labor market signals compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure, which increases the cost of capital and erodes real returns, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of high interest rates and rising inflation compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real retail and food services sales by more than 1% in a month signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenues and profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of decreasing retail and food services sales compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
